definition: The number $\boldsymbol{v} \cdot \boldsymbol{w} = v_{1}w_{1} + v_{2}w_{2} + v_{3}w_{3}$, found by multiplying matching components and adding, which also equals $\lvert\boldsymbol{v}\rvert\lvert\boldsymbol{w}\rvert\cos\theta$ where $\theta$ is the angle between the vectors; for non-zero vectors it is $0$ exactly when they are perpendicular.

The vector $\boldsymbol{v} \times \boldsymbol{w} = \lvert\boldsymbol{v}\rvert\lvert\boldsymbol{w}\rvert\sin\theta\,\boldsymbol{n}$, where $\theta$ is the angle between $\boldsymbol{v}$ and $\boldsymbol{w}$ and $\boldsymbol{n}$ is the unit vector perpendicular to both given by the right-hand screw rule (curl the fingers of your right hand from $\boldsymbol{v}$ towards $\boldsymbol{w}$ and your thumb points along $\boldsymbol{n}$); its length $\lvert\boldsymbol{v} \times \boldsymbol{w}\rvert$ is the area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides $\boldsymbol{v}$ and $\boldsymbol{w}$, and $\boldsymbol{w} \times \boldsymbol{v} = -(\boldsymbol{v} \times \boldsymbol{w})$.

term: component of a vector in a direction
definition: For a non-zero vector $\boldsymbol{b}$, the component of $\boldsymbol{a}$ in the direction of $\boldsymbol{b}$ is the scalar $\frac{\boldsymbol{a} \cdot \boldsymbol{b}}{\lvert\boldsymbol{b}\rvert} = \lvert\boldsymbol{a}\rvert\cos\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between them (negative when $\theta > 90^{\circ}$), and the component perpendicular to $\boldsymbol{b}$, in the plane of the two vectors, is $\frac{\lvert\boldsymbol{a} \times \boldsymbol{b}\rvert}{\lvert\boldsymbol{b}\rvert} = \lvert\boldsymbol{a}\rvert\sin\theta$.
